title: Mastering System Design: Building a High-Throughput Rate Limiter in Distributed Architectures
description: An in-depth engineering blueprint for designing production-ready distributed rate limiters. Compares Token Bucket, Sliding Window Counter algorithms, Redis Lua script implementations, handling race conditions, and interview tradeoffs.

faq.question: What is the best rate limiting algorithm for distributed systems?
faq.answer: Sliding Window Counter combined with Redis Lua scripts provides the best balance between memory efficiency, accuracy, and handling burst traffic in distributed environments.

faq.question: How do you prevent race conditions in a Redis rate limiter?
faq.answer: Execute rate limiting counter operations inside atomic Redis Lua scripts or use Redis transactions (MULTI/EXEC) to eliminate race conditions across distributed API servers.

title: Mastering Sliding Window Technique in Data Structures & Algorithms (C++ & TypeScript)
description: A definitive guide to mastering fixed and dynamic sliding window patterns in DSA. Includes step-by-step intuition, time complexity analysis, C++ STL code, and LeetCode problem walkthroughs.

faq.question: When should I use the Sliding Window pattern instead of Two Pointers?
faq.answer: Sliding Window is used when dealing with contiguous subarrays or substrings where you need to track a property (sum, max, unique characters) over a window of length K or variable size.

faq.question: What is the time complexity of the Sliding Window technique?
faq.answer: Sliding Window reduces nested O(N^2) brute force loops to linear O(N) time complexity because both left and right pointers traverse the array at most once.

title: Building Production-Grade Microservices with Next.js 15, Docker & Kubernetes
description: A complete DevOps playbook for containerizing Next.js 15 App Router applications using standalone multi-stage Dockerfiles, Docker Compose orchestrations, and Kubernetes (K8s) EKS deployment manifests.

faq.question: Why use Next.js standalone output mode for Docker containers?
faq.answer: Next.js standalone mode automatically traces dependencies and creates a minimal node_modules payload, reducing Docker image size from ~1GB to under 120MB.

faq.question: How do you handle environment variables in Next.js Docker images?
faq.answer: Build-time variables (NEXT_PUBLIC_*) are injected during docker build, while server-side runtime variables are mounted via Kubernetes ConfigMaps and Secrets.
